name: Anatomical terminology
description: The language of anatomy: the anatomical position, directions, planes, body regions and cavities, joint movements and the prefixes, suffixes and word roots used to build medical terms. A good first chapter, and a useful reference for every other one.

questions.prompt: Which is the standard anatomical position?
answers: Standing upright, facing forward, arms at the sides with the palms forward
Upright, facing front, palms forward, feet together
wrong: Lying on the back with the palms down
Standing with the palms facing the thighs and facing sideways
questions.explanation: Every direction is described as if the body were in this position, whatever its real position.

questions.prompt: Which term means towards the front of the body?
questions.explanation: The navel is anterior to the spine.

questions.prompt: Which term means towards the back of the body?
Which term means above, or towards the head?
questions.explanation: The head is superior to the neck.

questions.prompt: Which term means below, or towards the feet?
Which term means nearer to the midline of the body?
questions.explanation: The nose is medial to the ears.

questions.prompt: Which term means farther from the midline of the body?
questions.explanation: The ears are lateral to the eyes. In the anatomical position the thumb is the lateral digit of the hand.

questions.prompt: Which term means nearer to the point of attachment of a limb to the trunk?
questions.explanation: The elbow is proximal to the wrist.

questions.prompt: Which term means farther from the point of attachment of a limb to the trunk?
questions.explanation: The fingers are distal to the wrist.

questions.prompt: Which term means nearer to the surface of the body?
questions.explanation: The skin is superficial to the muscles.

questions.prompt: Which term means farther from the surface of the body?
questions.explanation: The ribs are deep to the skin.

questions.prompt: What does 'ipsilateral' mean?
answers: On the same side of the body
wrong: On the opposite side of the body
On both sides of the body
questions.explanation: The right hand and the right foot are ipsilateral.

questions.prompt: What does 'contralateral' mean?
answers: On the opposite side of the body
wrong: On the same side of the body
questions.explanation: The right arm and the left leg are contralateral.

questions.prompt: Which plane divides the body into left and right parts?
questions.explanation: A sagittal plane through the midline is the midsagittal (median) plane.

questions.prompt: Which plane divides the body into front (anterior) and back (posterior) parts?
questions.explanation: Named after the crown, as a tiara would sit on the head.

questions.prompt: Which plane divides the body into upper (superior) and lower (inferior) parts?
questions.explanation: A CT scan shows transverse slices.

questions.prompt: Another name for a cross-section (a transverse slice) is…
What is the difference between prone and supine?
answers: Prone is lying face down; supine is lying face up
Prone: face down. Supine: face up
wrong: Prone is lying face up; supine is lying face down
Prone is lying on the side
questions.explanation: A memory aid: you can hold a bowl of soup in your supine hand.

questions.prompt: Which terms describe the front and the back of the hand?
questions.explanation: In the foot the sole is plantar and the top is dorsal.

questions.prompt: What is the term for the sole of the foot?
What are the two main divisions of the body?
questions.explanation: The appendicular part includes the girdles.

questions.prompt: Which body cavity at the back holds the brain and the spinal cord?
answers: The dorsal cavity (cranial and spinal cavities)
questions.explanation: The cranial cavity holds the brain; the vertebral (spinal) cavity holds the cord.

questions.prompt: What are the two main parts of the ventral body cavity?
questions.explanation: They are separated by the diaphragm.

questions.prompt: What is the central part of the thoracic cavity, between the lungs, called?
questions.explanation: It holds the heart, great vessels, trachea, oesophagus and thymus.

questions.prompt: Which cavities surround each of the lungs?
questions.explanation: A thin film of fluid reduces friction.

questions.prompt: Which cavity surrounds the heart?
What is the membrane that lines the abdominal cavity and covers many of its organs?
questions.explanation: The parietal layer lines the wall; the visceral layer covers the organs.

questions.prompt: What are the two layers of a serous membrane called?
questions.explanation: With a thin space of fluid between them.

questions.prompt: Which of these organs is retroperitoneal, lying behind the peritoneum?
questions.explanation: Others are the pancreas (mostly), the duodenum (mostly), the aorta and the inferior vena cava.

questions.prompt: Into how many quadrants is the abdomen commonly divided, and by what?
answers: Four, by a vertical and a horizontal line through the navel
wrong: Nine, by two vertical and two horizontal lines
questions.explanation: Right upper, left upper, right lower and left lower.

questions.prompt: In which abdominal quadrant is most of the liver?
questions.explanation: The gallbladder is also in the right upper quadrant.

questions.prompt: In which abdominal quadrant is the appendix usually found?
questions.explanation: The pain of appendicitis ends up here, at McBurney's point.

questions.prompt: In which abdominal quadrant is the spleen?
questions.explanation: With most of the stomach.

questions.prompt: Into how many regions is the abdomen divided in the more detailed scheme?
questions.explanation: Right hypochondriac, epigastric, left hypochondriac; right lumbar, umbilical, left lumbar; right iliac (inguinal), hypogastric (pubic), left iliac.

questions.prompt: Which of the nine regions is directly above the umbilical region, over the stomach?
What is the name of the region of the arm between the shoulder and the elbow?
questions.explanation: The antebrachium is the forearm, between the elbow and the wrist.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the region of the forearm?
Which region is the hollow behind the knee?
questions.explanation: The cubital fossa is the hollow in front of the elbow.

questions.prompt: What is the armpit called in anatomy?
What is the name for the region of the eye?
questions.explanation: The cheek is buccal, the ear region is otic.

questions.prompt: What do 'cephalic' and 'cervical' mean?
answers: Of the head and of the neck
wrong: Of the neck and of the chest
Of the head and of the arm
Of the heart and of the neck
questions.explanation: The cervix is also 'the neck' of the uterus.

questions.prompt: Which regions are the chest and the lower back?
What is the groin called?
What is the region of the buttock called?
What does the prefix 'hypo-' mean?
questions.explanation: Hypothermia, hypoglycaemia.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix 'hyper-' mean?
questions.explanation: Hypertension, hyperthyroidism.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix 'peri-' mean?
questions.explanation: Pericardium: around the heart.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix 'endo-' mean?
questions.explanation: Endocardium: inside the heart.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix 'epi-' mean?
questions.explanation: Epidermis: upon the dermis.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix 'sub-' mean?
questions.explanation: Subcutaneous: under the skin.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix 'inter-' mean?
questions.explanation: Intercostal muscles lie between the ribs.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix 'intra-' mean?
questions.explanation: Intracellular: inside the cell.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix 'retro-' mean?
questions.explanation: Retroperitoneal: behind the peritoneum.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix 'para-' mean?
questions.explanation: Parathyroid glands lie beside the thyroid.

questions.prompt: What does 'brady-' mean?
questions.explanation: Bradycardia is a slow heart rate. Tachycardia is a fast one.

questions.prompt: What does the suffix '-itis' mean?
questions.explanation: Appendicitis, arthritis.

questions.prompt: What does the suffix '-ectomy' mean?
questions.explanation: Appendectomy.

questions.prompt: What does the suffix '-ostomy' mean?
questions.explanation: Colostomy: an opening of the colon on the abdominal wall.

questions.prompt: What does the suffix '-otomy' mean?
questions.explanation: Laparotomy.

questions.prompt: What does the suffix '-plasty' mean?
questions.explanation: Rhinoplasty.

questions.prompt: What does the suffix '-algia' mean?
questions.explanation: Neuralgia: nerve pain.

questions.prompt: What does the suffix '-oma' usually mean?
questions.explanation: Not always cancer: a lipoma is a benign fatty lump.

questions.prompt: What does the suffix '-aemia' (-emia) refer to?
questions.explanation: Anaemia, hyperglycaemia.

questions.prompt: What does the suffix '-uria' refer to?
questions.explanation: Haematuria: blood in the urine.

questions.prompt: Which word root refers to the heart?
questions.explanation: Cardiology.

questions.prompt: Which word root refers to the liver?
questions.explanation: Hepatitis.

questions.prompt: Which word root refers to the kidney?
questions.explanation: 'Renal' also refers to the kidney.

questions.prompt: Which word root refers to the stomach?
Which word root refers to the nerve?
Which word root refers to the bone?
Which word root refers to a joint?
Which word root refers to muscle?
questions.explanation: Myocardium is the heart muscle.

questions.prompt: Which word root refers to the skin?
questions.explanation: 'Cutaneous' also refers to the skin.

questions.prompt: Which word root refers to the lung?
Which word root refers to the blood?
Which word root refers to the cell?
questions.explanation: Histo- refers to tissue.

questions.prompt: What is a foramen?
answers: A hole in a bone, for a nerve or vessel to pass through
wrong: A cavity in a bone filled with air
questions.explanation: The foramen magnum is the large hole in the occipital bone.

questions.prompt: What is a bony process?
answers: A projecting part of a bone
questions.explanation: Examples: the spinous process of a vertebra, the mastoid process.

questions.prompt: What is a fossa?
questions.explanation: The popliteal fossa, the temporal fossa.

questions.prompt: What is a sulcus (and, in the brain, a fissure)?
questions.explanation: Between the gyri of the cerebral cortex.

questions.prompt: What is a tuberosity?
answers: A large rounded projection on a bone, often for a tendon
questions.explanation: The tibial tuberosity, where the patellar ligament attaches.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a tendon and a ligament?
answers: A tendon joins muscle to bone; a ligament joins bone to bone
Tendon: muscle to bone. Ligament: bone to bone
wrong: A tendon joins bone to bone; a ligament joins muscle to bone
A tendon joins muscle to muscle
questions.explanation: Ligaments hold the joints together.

questions.prompt: What is the 'origin' of a muscle?
answers: The attachment that does not move (usually proximal)
wrong: The attachment that moves when the muscle contracts
questions.explanation: The insertion is the attachment on the moving bone.

questions.prompt: What is flexion?
answers: Bending, decreasing the angle at a joint
A decrease in the angle between two bones
wrong: Straightening, increasing the angle at a joint
questions.explanation: Extension is the opposite.

questions.prompt: What is abduction?
answers: Moving a limb away from the midline
Movement away from the body's midline
wrong: Moving a limb towards the midline
questions.explanation: Adduction moves the limb towards the midline. A memory aid: an abductor takes it away.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between pronation and supination of the forearm?
answers: Pronation turns the palm down (backward); supination turns it up (forward)
Pronation: palm down; supination: palm up
wrong: Pronation turns the palm up; supination turns it down
Pronation bends the elbow; supination straightens it
Pronation spreads the fingers; supination closes them
questions.explanation: In the anatomical position the forearm is supinated.

questions.prompt: What is eversion of the foot?
questions.explanation: Inversion turns it inwards. An inversion injury is the common ankle sprain.

questions.prompt: Which movement of the foot pulls the toes up towards the shin?
questions.explanation: Plantar flexion points the toes down, as in standing on tiptoe.

tests.why: Anatomical position, directions and planes of the body.

tests.name: Chapter quiz
tests.why: Thirty questions from the whole chapter, marked at the end, like an end-of-unit test.

tests.name: Recall without choices
tests.why: Type each answer from memory, starting with the ones due for review. Small typos are forgiven.
